content: Iron(II) oxide, also referred to as ferrous oxide or ferrous iron, is one of the various oxides of iron. It appears as a black-colored powder and has the chemical formula FeO. This compound is composed of the chemical element iron in the +2 oxidation state, chemically bonded to oxygen. Its naturally occurring mineral form is called wüstite, a term often used interchangeably with ferrous oxide. Iron(II) oxide is an example of a non-stoichiometric compound, meaning the ratio of its constituent elements, iron and oxygen, can vary due to the presence of crystallographic vacancies. This compound is highly unstable and prone to oxidation, readily corroding into Iron(III) oxide (Fe₂O₃). It is important to note that Iron(II) oxide is distinct from rust, which typically consists of hydrated Iron(III) oxide, also known as ferric oxide. Iron(II) oxide is utilized as a pigment and has been approved by the FDA for use in cosmetics. Additionally, it is incorporated into certain tattoo inks.
